atoms.text: One cool morning, the graceful and hungry heron searched for her breakfast in the shallows of a river. Her eyes were sharp, and her beak was ready. “I’m going to find the perfect fish, and only then am I going to strike!” she thought to herself.

atoms.text:
A small fish swam through her legs, but she held herself back. “I can do better!” she thought and waited a little longer.

Another fish swam by, this one just a bit bigger than the first. She thought, “You’re not worth my time, either! I am going to find the perfect fish, so I’ll be full all day.”

atoms.text: Soon, the sun was high in the sky and the lovely heron had still not had her breakfast. “Why aren’t there any fish here?” she complained. But all the fish had already gone to deeper water to escape the heat of the sun.
atoms.sound: ssml:Soon, the sun was high in the sky and the lovely heron had still not had her breakfast.<voice voice='f2'><prosody rate = '90%'> “Why aren’t there any fish here?”</voice></prosody> she complained. But all the fish had already gone to deeper water to escape the heat of the sun.

atoms.text: “There just aren’t any fish today! I guess I will have to eat snails for breakfast. I hate snails!” said the heron. She found some snails to munch on, though none of them were as tasty or filling as even the smallest fish would have been.
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voice='f2'><prosody rate = '90%'>“There just aren’t any fish today! I guess I will have to eat snails for breakfast. I hate snails!”</voice></prosody> said the heron. She found some snails to munch on, though none of them were as tasty or filling as even the smallest fish would have been.

atoms.a: Why couldn’t the heron find any fish for breakfast?
b: The fish were hiding from her.
++The fish had gone to deeper water because it was too hot.

atoms.a: Why do you think the heron decided to eat snails instead?
b: ++because none of the fish she saw were big enough

atoms.a: What do you think the word filling means in the text?
b: something that makes the heron bigger

atoms.a: What do you think the lesson or moral of this story is?
b: Treat others as you want to be treated.
++If you are too hard to please, you may end up with something worse.

feedback.wrong: That’s not quite right. The heron was not mean to others.
